newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on soybean gains, forecast.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on soybean gains, forecast.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures ended higher on Thursday, lifted by late gains in soybeans and by perceptions the market had already put in harvest lows, pit sources said.
"I think people are making a case that the wheat is bottoming out, because it usually does at this time of year," said Jack Scoville, analyst with the Price Group brokerage in Chicago.
"Also, we've got rain in the forecast for the weekend which could keep cutting slow. There's talk of disease starting to pick up in the soft red crops."
Harvest in Texas hard red winter was said to be progressing quickly but cash sources gave mixed reviews to early yields and quality.

Lackluster weekly USDA export sales pressured the market early. The U.S. Department of Agriculture put net old and new crop wheat sales at 423,600 tonnes. That estimate fell below trade expectations for sales of 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
The International Grains Council upped its estimate for China wheat production to 112 million tonnes and said China's imports would fall by three million tonnes to four million.
CBOT SRW wheat ended 3-1/4 to 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher with July up 2-1/4 at $3.56.

Other bearish factors on the day included Sparks Companies' estimate for 1997 U.S. winter wheat production and news a wheat barter deal with North Korea had fallen through. Sparks, the Memphis-based analytical firm, reportedly upped its production figure to 1.576 million bushels.

Cargill Inc said it called off a wheat barter deal after North Korea failed to meet its part of the bargain to supply zinc in exchange for 20,000 tonnes of wheat. Cargill had received U.S. approval to sell up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat or rice to North Korea.
On the day, LIT bought two million bushels July and SAK Futures bought one million July.
In options, ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp sold 200 July $3.50 puts at 6-1/4 cents and Prudential Securities sold 200 December $3.50 puts at 12 to 13 cents.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 19,355.
